plan.summary: BRO-4623 part 8: replace 'Trade press / deep research synthesis' capitalization source lines with the outlet that reported each figure, remove the A Beautiful Noise and Redwood figures (no press or SEC source found), fix Some Like It Hot's note (it did not win Best Musical), and drop unsourced weekly-cost estimates from the notes touched.
steps: Checked 2026-10-04: Some Like It Hot $19.5M (Broadway Journal, Sep 28, 2023); Paradise Square up to $15M (The Hollywood Reporter, Jul 11, 2022); Into the Woods $4M (Broadway Journal, Aug 25, 2023); Tommy $15.7M (Rolling Stone citing the NYT, Jun 26, 2024); Funny Girl $16.5M (Deadline, Aug 7, 2023); Frozen around $35M (The Hollywood Reporter, May 14, 2020).
Single-outlet figures kept with attribution: The Music Man $24M (NYT, Sep 13, 2022, quoted by ArtsJournal and Queerty); Pretty Woman $17M (Forbes, Aug 23, 2018).

No figure found for A Beautiful Noise (Deadline, Broadway News, Playbill closing articles; Broadway Journal; SEC search) or Redwood (Deadline, THR, NBC NY closing articles; SEC search), so both capitalizations become null.
Chess: SEC Form D/A (Chess Champion LLC, Jan 5, 2026) shows $15M fully sold; the source line drops internal research notes.

actions.oldValue: Broadway musical that opened Nov 2022 and closed Dec 2023. Capitalized at $19.5M with ~$900K weekly running costs. Despite strong reviews and Tony wins (Best Musical), could not sustain ticket sales and closed without recouping. Grossed $70.7M over 440 performances.
actions.newValue: Musical that opened Dec 2022 and closed Dec 30, 2023 without recouping its $19.5M capitalization (Broadway Journal). Nominated for Best Musical and won four 2023 Tony Awards, including Best Leading Actor in a Musical for J. Harrison Ghee. Grossed $70.7M over 440 performances.

actions.oldValue: Jukebox musical about Neil Diamond that opened Dec 2022 and closed June 2024. Capitalized at ~$20M with ~$1.09M weekly running costs. Despite moderate grosses (~$700K-$900K weekly), the high operating costs and capitalization meant it closed well short of recoupment after 18 months.
actions.newValue: Neil Diamond jukebox musical that opened Dec 2022 and closed Jun 2024 without announcing recoupment. Its Broadway capitalization was not reported.
The Hollywood Reporter (Jul 2022): capitalized for up to $15M

actions.oldValue: Original musical that opened April 2022 and closed July 2022 after only 109 performances. Capitalized at ~$15M with ~$599K weekly running costs. Despite a Joaquina Kalukango Tony win, very poor ticket sales ($200K-$350K weekly gross vs $599K breakeven) led to rapid closure and near-total loss of investment.
actions.newValue: Original musical that opened Apr 2022 and closed Jul 2022 without recouping. Capitalized for up to $15M (The Hollywood Reporter). Joaquina Kalukango won the 2022 Tony for Best Leading Actress in a Musical, but weak sales and reports of late payments led to an early closing.

actions.oldValue: Encores! transfer revival that opened June 2022 at the St. James. Low $4M capitalization (Encores! transfer, minimal set) and strong demand allowed recoupment in approximately 3-4 months. Extended multiple times through closing in Jan 2023. Grossed $48.6M over 293 performances — exceptional ROI on the modest investment.
actions.newValue: Encores! revival that transferred to the St. James in summer 2022 and closed in Jan 2023 after extensions. Low $4M capitalization; Broadway Journal lists it among the 2022-23 season's commercial winners. Grossed $48.6M over 293 performances.

actions.oldValue: Disney Theatrical production that opened Mar 2018. One of the most expensive Broadway musicals at ~$35M. Had $63M advance by opening. Grossed $1.5-2M/week during holidays, ran 825 performances with strong sales. COVID shutdown in Mar 2020 halted the run; Disney announced May 2020 it would not reopen. Estimated ~$120-130M total gross — impressive but insufficient to recoup the massive capitalization given 2 years of ~$1M/week costs.
actions.newValue: Disney Theatrical production that opened Mar 2018 and played 825 performances. Capitalized at around $35M (The Hollywood Reporter). Disney said in May 2020 it would not reopen after the COVID shutdown. Disney rarely confirms profitability and no recoupment was announced.

actions.oldValue: Idina Menzel star vehicle. $16M cap. Weekly nut ~$650K (Menzel's star salary was major expense). Grossed $800-900K at ~90% capacity in spring, yielding small weekly profits, but sales softened after Tony shutout. Closed May 18, 2025 after only 4 months. Menzel was only contracted through May — couldn't extend with replacement. Investors recovered estimated 20-30% of capital. Roundabout co-presented earlier Off-Broadway workshop.
actions.newValue: Idina Menzel star vehicle. Closed May 18, 2025 after receiving no Tony nominations (Deadline). No capitalization reported and no recoupment announced.
